disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is characterized by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and a distorted perception of body weight or shape or undue influence of weight/shape on self-evaluation. Patients often deny the seriousness of their low body weight and may present with rigid rules around food, compulsive exercise, or other weight-control behaviors. Onset is typically in adolescence or young adulthood but can occur later in life, often in the context of perfectionism, need for control, or precipitating stressors around body image, health, or life transitions. It is distinguished from other eating disorders by the combination of underweight status with cognitive overvaluation of thinness and active restriction, rather than recurrent binge/purge episodes at normal or high weight as seen in bulimia nervosa or binge-eating disorder.

narrative.personality: Detail-oriented and highly disciplined, Detrail is a routine-driven, competitive worker who takes pride in self-sufficiency and mentoring others while quietly holding himself to very high standards.
narrative.stressor: Detrail’s preoccupation with physical conditioning began when his company shifted contracts to a large luxury complex, where he found himself constantly interacting with upscale tenants and younger, visibly fit maintenance techs he was now supervising. Around the same time, a minor back strain from lifting an HVAC unit led his employer’s occupational health provider to warn him about his weight and "longevity" in this physically demanding role, which he internalized as a threat to his career plans of becoming a facilities manager and eventually launching his own firm. His meticulous, all-or-nothing temperament translated into increasingly rigid rules around eating and training, initially framed as a disciplined "cut" to be leaner and more agile for work and basketball, but gradually crowding out his enjoyment of food and social meals he used to cook for friends and mentees. Over months, he kept tightening these routines despite coworkers and mentees commenting that he looked "too run down," and he finally agreed to psychiatric evaluation after an occupational health visit flagged his markedly low weight and recommended he address the underlying beliefs driving his extreme pursuit of leanness.
narrative.chief_complaint: “They keep telling me I’m way too thin for my job, and now work says I need to get checked out because my weight’s gotten so low.”

narrative.personality: Eric is a creatively driven, competitively curious muralist who balances meticulous organization with a constant push to reinvent himself and stand out in the community art scene.
narrative.stressor: As Eric moved into his early sixties, he became increasingly aware of being one of the oldest artists at festivals and residencies, where curators and sponsors subtly favored younger, "edgier" bodies and aesthetics in promotional materials. A casual comment at a regional art festival, where someone praised a much younger muralist for having the "lean, urban look" that supposedly matched contemporary street art, stuck with him and fed into a longstanding competitive streak and fear of becoming irrelevant. He began scrutinizing photos of himself in gallery press, comparing his appearance to slimmer peers and telling himself that refining his body shape was another artistic discipline, slowly tightening his eating and exercise routines under the guise of "staying light for the scaffolding" and projecting a sharper profile in photographs. Over time, worries about how his body looked in VR installations, workshop demos, and promotional shots started overshadowing the joy of painting, and he sought psychiatric care after friends in his cycling group and a workshop participant both expressed concern that his intense focus on looking thin and "on-brand" for his art seemed to be taking over his life.
narrative.chief_complaint: “Lately I can’t stop fixating on how my body looks in photos and at shows, and it feels like my whole sense of worth as an artist depends on staying lean enough.”

narrative.personality: Derek is a solitary, methodical man who values control, safety, and routine, often immersing himself in detailed maintenance tasks and logs to keep his world predictable.
narrative.stressor: Derek’s shift toward rigid control over his eating began after a routine physical for his commercial driving certification revealed mildly elevated cholesterol and blood pressure, which the occupational physician warned could threaten his long-term clearance if not addressed. Already highly focused on safety and prevention in his work, he interpreted this as a serious warning that his body was another machine that could fail catastrophically if not tightly managed, and he began reading obsessively about "clean" diets and heart-healthy regimens, tracking every calorie and meal in the same meticulous way he logged oil changes and hydraulic checks. Initially, he framed the changes as a sensible health tune-up, but his naturally anxious, perfectionistic streak led him to continually narrow what he considered "safe" foods, skipping family meals and delaying dinner to re-measure portions or revise his food logs in order to feel in control. Over time, his wife and adult children noticed he was eating less and less and seemed increasingly distressed if his strict routines were disrupted, and he finally agreed to psychiatric evaluation when a follow-up occupational medical exam documented marked weight loss and his supervisor questioned whether his physical condition was compatible with safely operating heavy equipment.
narrative.chief_complaint: “I’ve cut back more and more on what I eat to keep my health and job safe, but now they’re saying I’m not eating enough and my weight’s gotten too low.”
